=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:_trusted_run_link_comment (around lines 1774-1779); _verify_label_run_refs (around lines 1801-1826); build_issue_payload (lines 730-738) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: For consumer-repository label escalations, a trusted human comment can vouch for an unrelated failed run whose display title collides with the issue title.
  WHY: The verifier relies solely on the trusted comment for issue-to-run association, then fetches the unrelated run's jobs and logs for diagnosis.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Accept run references only from provenance-verified automation records, and verify each run's failure and association with the escalated issue before fetching logs." (issue #6514)
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py::_trusted_run_link_comment and scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py::_verify_label_run_refs (specifically the linked_ids collection that turns a trusted human comment into sole proof of run-to-issue association)
  Evidence of absence: The implementation's _trusted_run_link_comment treats any OWNER / MEMBER / COLLABORATOR comment as authoritative vouch for a run link, and tests at tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:4099-4101 lock that behavior in: `assert check(payload, {"500": unrelated}, [link(CONSUMER_REPO, 500, "maintainer", "MEMBER")])["run_refs"]` and the github-actions[bot] sibling assertion explicitly demonstrate that human OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR comments vouch for an unrelated failed run. The intake therefore accepts human-authored comments as provenance-verified records, even though the audit's recommendation restricted the trust surface to automation records. The fix removed the weak title-equality fallback but did not narrow the trust surface from "trusted commenter" to "trusted automation commenter," so the recommendation is only partially met.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Accept run references only from provenance-verified automation records, and verify each run's failure and association with the escalated issue before fetching logs."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py::_trusted_run_link_comment (lines 1771-1779) and _verify_label_run_refs (lines 1797-1838)
  Evidence of absence: The implementation accepts run links from any OWNER, MEMBER, or COLLABORATOR comment in consumer repositories (line 1774: `comment.get("author_association") not in PHASE_REPORT_TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS`), not only from provenance-verified automation records. The existing phase_failure provenance check (lines 485-499) is stricter: it requires the comment to start with a specific phase-failure prefix (PHASE_FAILURE_COMMENT_PREFIXES), proving it is automation-generated, before trusting it. The label-escalation path has no equivalent automation-prefix check — a human MEMBER comment with any run URL suffices. For consumer-repo issue reports, a MEMBER could link an unrelated failed run (that the reporter already title-matched) and have its logs fetched for diagnosis. The run's logs would then enter the diagnosis prompt and could be reproduced in the heal issue. This requires a trusted actor, so the severity is limited, but the recommendation's "automation records" wording is not fully satisfied.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:_verify_label_run_refs, lines 1815-1826 (PR association check)
  PROBLEM: For issue reports, a trusted comment link is the only association proof; there is no GitHub-native issue-to-run association.
  WHY: Requiring an automation prefix on issue-report comments would narrow acceptance to automation records as the recommendation suggests; consumer-repository PR reports retain the PR-association path.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
